comparison_note: Jev oracle variants share one algorithm; differences are sampling/operations, not extraction gains. Comparisons with old methods change workflow/model/policy.

extraction_diagnostics.note: Duplicates are repeated normalized text or a second alias for an already matched gold. Merges, splits and scope loss require the separate semantic audit.

failure_inclusive_quality.false_support_note: C/U gold matched to SUPPORTED, divided by all C/U gold. Missing/error claims remain in the denominator, never count as false support; read with judgment coverage and request failures.
failure_inclusive_quality.macro_f1_note: Fixed three-class mean; null if any class has no gold or prediction.

routing.alignment_note: Oracle uses direct input identity. End-to-end uses frozen verdict-blind text alignment; unaligned and missing traces remain explicit, not semantically certified errors. Automatic coverage counts Jev-origin decisions; deterministic empty-context origins are separate.

uncertainty.limitations: Family sample sensitivity only; excludes annotation bias and unobserved model randomness. Degenerate intervals do not demonstrate zero uncertainty. Undefined draws are counted.

limitations: Real public-source English benchmark; answer origins are reported separately. Document familiarity and related sources can bias results. AI annotation can share model biases; independent and human review states are recorded separately.
Strict whitespace-only text/alias matching can undercount valid paraphrases; unmatched predictions are retained.
Literal quotation validity and gold-span coverage do not establish semantic entailment.
A gold span must be contained in one returned quote; alternate sufficient quotations may be undercounted.
Bootstrap intervals describe case/family sample sensitivity, not annotation uncertainty or model randomness.
Offline protocol fixtures are not live model measurements. Subscription tokens have no inferred dollar price.
